criteria.intro: Der Prüfling benennt ethnische Minderheiten als besonders betroffene Gruppe und erläutert die Gründe hierfür, etwa:
bullets: explains that people of colour faced a higher mortality risk during the pandemic
points out that poverty and pre-existing health conditions such as diabetes increased vulnerability
names systemic racism as a contributing factor to unequal health outcomes
explains that stress and hypertension linked to social disadvantage further increased risk
notes that these factors are not evenly distributed across the population

criteria.intro: Der Prüfling benennt Menschen in sozial belasteten Lebenssituationen (Isolation, häusliche Gewalt, Wohnungslosigkeit) als besonders betroffene Gruppe und erläutert die Gründe hierfür, etwa:
bullets: explains that people living alone experienced heightened loneliness during lockdown
points out that individuals in unsafe home environments were at greater risk due to increased time spent with abusers
names homelessness as a factor that made safe isolation impossible
explains that some people found the lockdown itself frightening rather than safe
notes that a lack of social contact worsened people's emotional wellbeing

criteria.intro: Der Prüfling benennt Kinder ohne digitale Ausstattung als besonders betroffene Gruppe und erläutert die Gründe hierfür, etwa:
bullets: explains that children without Wi-Fi or a computer could not take part in digital learning
points out that this lack of access limited their educational opportunities during lockdown
names the resulting educational disadvantage as a long-term consequence
explains that this inequality is linked to their families' financial situation

criteria.intro: Der Prüfling entwickelt eine schlüssige These, die aufzeigt, wie Register, sprachrhetorische Mittel und Struktur des Gedichts zusammenwirken, um die intendierte Bedeutung zu vermitteln, z. B.:
bullets: points out that register, stylistic devices and structure jointly expose social inequality behind the seemingly unifying phrase "we are in this together"
argues that the poem uses these means to move the reader from critical questioning towards a shared, hopeful vision
explains that language and form work together to challenge an oversimplified notion of collective experience
illustrates that the poem's persuasive effect relies on the interplay of an accessible register, striking rhetorical devices and a purposeful three-part structure

criteria.intro: Der Prüfling analysiert die Wirkung des Registers auf die intendierte Bedeutung des Gedichts, z. B.:
bullets: identifies the informal, conversational register created by direct address and rhetorical questions ("Are you the 'we' who's missing your mates?", l. 16)
notes how colloquial phrasing ("a funny thing to say", l. 34) creates intimacy between speaker and reader
points out that the shift to a more solemn, elevated register in the final stanza ("I pray so hard for a new world fashion", l. 42) underlines the poem's hopeful message
explains that the direct second-person address "you" throughout implicates the reader in the social critique
highlights that simple, everyday vocabulary makes the poem's political message accessible to a broad audience
illustrates how the conversational register mirrors the poem's claim that "togetherness" should include everyone, regardless of background

criteria.intro: Der Prüfling analysiert die Wirkung sprachrhetorischer Mittel auf die intendierte Bedeutung des Gedichts, z. B.:
bullets: identifies the anaphoric repetition of "we" throughout the poem, emphasising the central question of who is included in this collective pronoun
points out the recurring rhetorical questions ("Or are you a 'we' on the front-line?", l. 10) that force the reader to locate their own position
analyses the antithesis between privilege and hardship ("Higher survival if you are white", l. 11) to expose social inequality
explains the use of quotation marks around "we", "in" and "together" (l. 1, l. 21, l. 33) to foreground these key terms as contested concepts
notes the enumeration of hardships (poverty, diabetes, racism, stress, hypertension, l. 12–13) to illustrate the cumulative impact of inequality
illustrates the shift from bleak imagery ("This poem could be one of despair", l. 40) to hopeful imagery ("Where friendship and family thrive", l. 51) as a stylistic turning point

criteria.intro: Der Prüfling analysiert die Wirkung der Struktur des Gedichts auf die intendierte Bedeutung, z. B.:
bullets: identifies the tripartite structure following the three key words of the title phrase ("we", "in", "together")
points out that each section opens with a direct interrogation of the respective term, structuring the poem as a guided argument
explains the framing effect created by the repetition of the title phrase at the beginning (l. 1) and end (l. 59) of the poem
analyses the turning point marked by "So I will not leave it there" (l. 41), which structurally divides critique from vision
notes how the final stanza's accumulation of parallel "that"-clauses (l. 43–48) builds towards the poem's hopeful conclusion
illustrates how the structural progression from division to unity mirrors the poem's argument that genuine togetherness must be earned

criteria.intro: Der Prüfling nimmt begründet Stellung zu Pichais These, dass vielfältige Perspektiven zu besseren Diskussionen, Entscheidungen und Ergebnissen führen, z. B.:
bullets: assesses the validity of Pichai's claim with reference to concrete examples
discusses potential limitations or exceptions to the claim
differentiates between diversity as a value in itself and diversity as a means to better outcomes
evaluates whether diverse teams automatically lead to better decision-making
considers counterarguments to Pichai's optimistic view
reaches a balanced, well-reasoned conclusion on the quote's validity

criteria.intro: Der Prüfling bezieht die eigene Erfahrung und Herkunft nachvollziehbar in die Stellungnahme ein, z. B.:
bullets: illustrates the argument with a concrete example from personal experience
reflects on how their own background has shaped their view on diversity
connects personal experience to the broader claim made by Pichai
shows awareness of their own position of privilege or disadvantage
draws a general conclusion from the personal example
links the personal reflection back to the overall line of argument

criteria.intro: Der Prüfling stellt einen inhaltlich stimmigen Bezug zum Gedicht von Bristow her, z. B.:
bullets: draws on the poem's central idea of an unevenly shared "we" to support or challenge Pichai's claim
refers to specific examples of inequality mentioned in the poem ("Higher survival if you are white", l. 11)
connects the poem's call for genuine compassion (l. 43) to the value of diverse perspectives
uses the poem's vision of an "all inclusive" we (l. 48) to strengthen the argument
shows how the poem illustrates the consequences of excluding certain voices
integrates the poem's message coherently into the overall argument

criteria.intro: Der Prüfling stellt einen inhaltlich stimmigen Bezug zur im Gedicht geäußerten Kritik her, z. B.:
bullets: refers to the poem's critique of unevenly shared risks and hardships ("Factors not evenly shared", l. 14)
addresses the poem's criticism of unequal access to digital learning (l. 30–31)
takes up the poem's call for more compassion and equality (l. 43, l. 55)
uses the poem's central question "Who is the 'we'" (l. 4) to frame the letter's concern
refers to the poem's depiction of loneliness and domestic violence during lockdown (l. 24–25)
connects the poem's vision of an "all inclusive" we (l. 48) to the letter's demands

criteria.intro: Der Prüfling formuliert drei konkrete, nachvollziehbare Verbesserungsvorschläge, z. B.:
bullets: proposes a concrete measure to reduce educational inequality (e.g. free digital devices for low-income families)
suggests a policy addressing unequal healthcare access for disadvantaged groups
proposes support structures for people affected by domestic violence or isolation
formulates the suggestions in a persuasive, action-oriented way
prioritises the suggestions according to urgency
links each suggestion explicitly back to a problem raised in the poem

criteria.intro: Der Prüfling bezieht eigene Erfahrungen sowie im Unterricht behandelte Inhalte zu gender identity und sexual orientation nachvollziehbar ein, z. B.:
bullets: illustrates the argument with a concrete personal experience related to identity or inclusion
draws on the concept of the "white privilege backpack" (Peggy McIntosh) discussed in class to explain unearned advantages
reflects critically on their own position of privilege or disadvantage using this concept
connects classroom discussions on gender identity and sexual orientation to the letter's argument
shows awareness of intersecting forms of disadvantage (e.g. race, gender, class)
integrates the personal and classroom-based reflection coherently into the overall letter

criteria.intro: Der Prüfling richtet seinen Text konsequent und explizit im Sinne der Aufgabenstellung auf die Intention und den Adressaten aus.
Der Prüfling beachtet die Textsortenmerkmale der jeweils geforderten Zieltextformate.
Der Prüfling erstellt einen sachgerecht strukturierten Text.
Der Prüfling gestaltet seinen Text hinreichend ausführlich, aber ohne unnötige Wiederholungen und Umständlichkeiten.
Der Prüfling belegt seine Aussagen durch eine funktionale Verwendung von Verweisen und Zitaten.
Der Prüfling löst sich vom Wortlaut des Ausgangstextes und formuliert eigenständig.
Der Prüfling verwendet funktional einen sachlich wie stilistisch angemessenen und differenzierten allgemeinen und thematischen Wortschatz.
Der Prüfling verwendet einen funktional angemessenen Wortschatz zur Textproduktion und Textbesprechung.
Der Prüfling verwendet einen variablen und dem jeweiligen Zieltextformat angemessenen Satzbau.
Wortschatz — Der Prüfling beachtet die Normen der sprachlichen Korrektheit im Sinne einer gelingenden Kommunikation.
Grammatik
Orthografie
Der Prüfling erläutert Krafts Haltung zu Queerness und Geschlechteridentität im Shakespeare'schen Theater, etwa:
bullets: explains that Kraft sees a lot of queerness already inherent in Shakespeare's "As You Like It"
points out that gender-swapping and play with gender roles are central to the plot
explains that in Shakespeare's time all roles were played by male actors
illustrates the layered gender confusion: a male actor plays Rosalind, who then disguises herself as a man
explains that Rosalind and Celia, though cousins, are also one of the play's great love pairs
points out that many scenes play with typical gender roles and expose their absurdity
explains that Kraft describes this as full of subversive humour
mentions that Kraft chose the title "As You Fucking Like It" to signal that his production is not simply the original play

criteria.intro: Der Prüfling erläutert Krafts Haltung zur Liebe in Shakespeares Literatur und Theater, etwa:
bullets: explains that love is the main driving force of the plot
points out that, according to Kraft, love in Shakespeare is not bound to gender
illustrates that love appears as a powerful force affecting everyone equally
explains that despite this, the couples are ultimately sorted in a heteronormative way at the end, as is typical for the genre
points out that in Kraft's own version, this absurdity of heteronormative norms is exaggerated
explains that Kraft's production ultimately opens up marriage to everyone
mentions Kraft's wordplay on "kreuz und quer" and "kreuz und queer" to describe love's unpredictable nature
illustrates that love is portrayed as confusing yet universal

criteria.intro: Der Prüfling erläutert Krafts selbstgewählte Mission mit dem Stück, etwa:
bullets: explains that Kraft wants both his parents and his queer friends to be able to enjoy the play equally
points out that he aims to address drag fans as well as people who have never encountered drag before
explains that his goal is for the production to be enriching for everyone
illustrates that Kraft acknowledges this balancing act as sometimes difficult
explains that when it succeeds, a theatre evening can bring very different people together
mentions that Kraft finds this ability to unite different audiences deeply gratifying
points out that this mission reflects his broader interest in questions of identity across old and new works

criteria.intro: Der Prüfling richtet seinen Text konsequent und explizit auf die Intention und den Adressatenkreis im Sinne der Aufgabenstellung aus, berücksichtigt den situativen Kontext, beachtet die Textsortenmerkmale des geforderten Zieltextformats, erstellt einen sachgerecht strukturierten Text und gestaltet seinen Text hinreichend ausführlich, aber ohne unnötige Wiederholungen und Umständlichkeiten.

Der Prüfling löst sich vom Wortlaut des Ausgangstextes und formuliert eigenständig, ggf. unter Verwendung von Kompensationsstrategien, verwendet funktional einen sachlich wie stilistisch angemessenen und differenzierten allgemeinen, thematischen und Funktionswortschatz und verwendet einen variablen und dem jeweiligen Zieltextformat angemessenen Satzbau.
Der Prüfling beachtet die Normen der sprachlichen Korrektheit im Sinne einer gelingenden Kommunikation (Wortschatz, Grammatik, Orthografie).
